pr_title: Add proper EMP behavior to TS aircraft
pr_body:
This PR
- makes `Aircraft` pausable-conditional
- makes landed, EMP'd TS aircraft behave like EMP'd ground vehicles
- makes airborne TS aircraft crash when EMP'd

Closes #17096.
Fixes #16421.
pr_comments:
Really nice!

Some things I noticed:
- Airborne units don't get the visual overlay when EMP-ed
- Landed units can still be ordered to take off, but they will crash instantly.

> Airborne units don't get the visual overlay when EMP-ed

This will be a bit tricky to fix, since the tumbling aircraft husk is not the original aircraft, and we can't be sure that its spawner wasn't shot down by normal means. I'd like to leave that aspect for later.

> Landed units can still be ordered to take off, but they will crash instantly.

I'll look into that.

> > Airborne units don't get the visual overlay when EMP-ed
> 
> This will be a bit tricky to fix, since the tumbling aircraft husk is not the original aircraft, and we can't be sure that its spawner wasn't shot down by normal means. I'd like to leave that aspect for later.

Can't you base something on the framework which transfers the IronCurtain in RA from MCV to conyard?

It should be as simple as adding
```
TransferTimedExternalConditionOnTransform:
	Condition: empdisable
```

to the aircraft.

From https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/pull/17189#issuecomment-538766314, IMO it would be best if we could make `Aircraft` pausing replace `LandOnCondition` (and fix it so it actually works). Is that too much of a scope creep here?

> It should be as simple as adding `TransferTimedExternalConditionOnTransform` to the aircraft

Unfortunately it isn't, we need an equivalent for `SpawnActorOnDeath`, but that needs an equivalent of `void INotifyTransform.AfterTransform(Actor toActor)` first.

> From #17189 (comment), IMO it would be best if we could make Aircraft pausing replace LandOnCondition (and fix it so it actually works). Is that too much of a scope creep here?

Well I can try, might still shout for help or a deferral afterwards, though.

Rebased and updated.

- Enabled emp effect on husks by spawning a different husk when killed by EMP
- Fixed Harpy husk rotor offset
- Refactored `FallsToEarth` spin logic (the old one made aircraft spin way too fast)
- Removed `LandOnCondition` in favor of pausing, remove/comment out `KillsSelf` on any EMP-able TS aircraft to test

> Refactored FallsToEarth spin logic (the old one made aircraft spin way too fast)

A much more lenient option - even your setup is too fast for RA2 Kirov.
https://github.com/AttacqueSuperior/Engine/blob/master/OpenRA.Mods.AS/Traits/Air/FallsToEarthAS.cs#L25

- Landed EMP-ed aircraft still instantly crash when ordered to take off instead of staying put in the latest version.
- Landed aircraft get darkened when they are EMP-ed while airborne aircraft do not. They do get the proper overlay though.

>  - Infantry can enter / exit Orka transport when it's EMPed
> - EMP doesn't pause the rearming process

These issues are also still present. The former is also the case for APCs, so that might be out of scope here.

> Landed aircraft get darkened when they are EMP-ed while airborne aircraft do not. They do get the proper overlay though

I know it's technically inconsistent, but to me, the darkening has always mainly served as "you can't use this right now", indicating this will resume working after some time, while husks are mainly cosmetics as the original aircraft is already dead at that point.
Yes that makes perfect sense if you view the darkening as purely non-diegetic. I hadn't really looked at it that way.

Rebased and updated.

> Landed EMP-ed aircraft still instantly crash when ordered to take off instead of staying put in the latest version.

Fixed in c316111 (had to add a work-around to `Fly` activity, properly refactoring aircraft activities is out of scope for this PR).

> - Infantry can enter / exit Orka transport when it's EMPed
> - EMP doesn't pause the rearming process

I'm afraid both of these are out of scope for this PR.
`Cargo` isn't pausable-conditional (not conditional at all, actually), while the rearm part depends on my still-incomplete resupply refactor roadmap. 
Reloading ammo pools will eventually shift to `ReloadAmmoPool` entirely, but the minimum prerequisite for that is to grant a condition during resupply, and that's something I'd like to leave for a follow-up.
Updated, but this broke husk spawning and I have no idea why yet.

> Updated, but this broke husk spawning and I have no idea why yet.

This happens because `KillsSelf` kills the actor directly inside its `TraitEnabled`, which means that `INotifyKilled.Killed` runs in the middle of the `empdisabled` condition change notification. 

The rule reorganization means that the non-EMP `SpawnActorOnDeath` is notified first and disables itself. `KillsSelf`, then runs and kills the actor `SpawnActorOnDeath@EMP` is notified of the death and, because doesn't know about the condition change, is still disabled.

A new commit that wraps `KillsSelf`'s `Kill(self)` in a frame end task fixes the issue.
Updated. Tested both RA and TS, and both looked good to me now.
Updated, restored random spin direction (tested in TS) and fixed description.

issue_context.title: Aircraft trait is not conditional
issue_context.body: It is a problem in TS as aircraft can be EMPed. There's no way to stop an aircraft from moving and loading / unloading cargo
comments: Technically - EMP crashed aircrafts in TS which is already doable with triggering a `KillsSelf` so it should not be a problem there.

[LandOnCondition](https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/blob/bleed/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Air/Aircraft.cs#L154) should hopefully cover most other usecases. We could consider promoting this to the conditional (paused?) trait behaviour.

I tried adding `LandOnCondition: empdisable` on TS aircraft and when I give them a move order while they're EMPed they lift up and permanently freeze. They do not respond to any orders in that state even after the EMP effect wears off

`LandOnCondition` is broken beyond repair (I have no idea if it ever was functional) and is not currently used for anything. It should just be removed and maybe reimplemented from scratch if there is an actual usecase that cannot be done in any other way.

If we make EMP crash flying aircraft and leave it at that it would only be detrimental to gameplay. Aircraft are very expensive and losing a flock of them would usually lead to defeat. We need to have proper warnings and a longish delay on EMP cannon so you'd have time to react. I'll probably make a PR for adding this feature and we can figure out balance when TS is closer to release

It still would not make sense to have landed aircraft blowup so that issue remains

In standard TS gameplay EMP can't even affect units in air - neither the EMPCannon, neither the Mobile EMP could reach flying aircraft. The sole usecase of the EMP crash in TS was used by the Ion Storm, which crashed all flying units and sank the Hover MRLS in water.

Sure, landed aircraft just got disabled, but I presume that can be done with a `SpeedMultiplier: 0` for now.

If subterranean units go to the surface at the nearest available spot when EMPed, then it would also make sense for aircraft to land at the nearest available spot when EMPed. It would be less disproportionately punishing, but still allows it to be used meaningfully against airborne units.

This should be implemented by making `Aircraft` pausableConditional so it would work the same as `Mobile`.

It should work the same as `mobile`. 
As Graion said in the original EMP didn't work on airborne Aircraft. EMP should only hit landed ones and disable them. But I'm not saying that it shouldn't be possible to disable midair for modders though

review_comments: I just noticed that this is removing the random spin direction - all units will now spin anti-clockwise.

This regresses helicopter crashing in TD and RA, which rely on being able to spin up faster than their natural turn speed. The simple solution is to redefine `-1` to mean no limit, and have the TS aircraft yaml this to their turn speed (or IMO something like twice the spin speed would be better).

This causes a divide by zero crash at https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/blob/7a57f0e6ef3be227e04b005816847f6af1570fd8/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Activities/Air/Fly.cs#L257

if the aircraft is paused above terrain where it can't land.

Changing that to `return turnSpeed > 0 ? 45 * speed / turnSpeed : 0;` fixes the issue.
